column1: ‘Hypotheses,’ said Medawar in 1964, ‘are imaginative and inspirational in character’; they are ‘adventures of the mind’.
column2: 梅达沃在1964年说，假设“具有想象力，能给人以启发”，是“思想的探险”。
column7: adventures of the mind|n. 思想的探险

column1: He was arguing in favour of the position taken by Karl Popper in The Logic of Scientific Discovery (1972, 3rd edition) that the nature of scientific method is hypothetico-deductive and not, as is generally believed, inductive.
column2: 他是在支持卡尔·波普尔在《科学发现的逻辑》（1972年第三版）中提出的观点：科学方法本质上采用的是假设演绎法，有别于人们普遍以为的归纳法。
column10: hypothetico-deductive|adj. 运用假设演绎法的

column1: It is essential that you, as an intending researcher, understand the difference between these two interpretations of the research process so that you do not become discouraged or begin to suffer from a feeling of ‘cheating’ or not going about it the right way.
column2: 作为有志于从事研究的人，你必须理解这两种对研究过程的解释之间的区别，以免感到气馁，或产生‘作弊’或方法不当的错觉。

column1: The myth of scientific method is that it is inductive: that the formulation of scientific theory starts with the basic, raw evidence of the senses – simple, unbiased, unprejudiced observation.
column2: 科学方法的神话是：科学理论的形成始于感官所获得的原始、未经加工的、无偏见的、无成见的简单观察。

column1: Out of these sensory data – commonly referred to as ‘facts’ — generalisations will form.
column2: 从这些感官数据中，可以形成一些概括。

column1: The myth is that from a disorderly array of factual information an orderly, relevant theory will somehow emerge.
column2: 有一种误解，认为从一堆杂乱无章的事实信息中，会自然地涌现出一个有序且相关的理论。

column1: However, the starting point of induction is an impossible one.
column2: 然而，归纳法的起点是不可实现的。

column1: There is no such thing as an unbiased observation.
column2: 不存在没有偏见的观察。

column1: Every act of observation we make is a function of what we have seen or otherwise experienced in the past.
column2: 我们每一次的观察行为，都源于过去所见或所经历的经验。

column1: All scientific work of an experimental or exploratory nature starts with some expectation about the outcome.
column2: 所有具有实验性或探索性质的科学工作都始于对结果的某种预期。

column1: This expectation is a hypothesis.
column2: 这种预期是一种假设。

column1: Hypotheses provide the initiative and incentive for the inquiry and influence the method.
column2: 假设为研究提供了动力和激励，并影响了研究方法。

column1: It is in the light of an expectation that some observations are held to be relevant and some irrelevant, that one methodology is chosen and others discarded, that some experiments are conducted and others are not.
column2: 正是基于对某些观察相关而某些无关的预期，人们才会选择某种方法论而舍弃其他方法，从而进行一些实验而放弃另一些实验。

column1: Where is, your naive, pure and objective researcher now?
column2: 你那个天真、纯真且客观的研究人员现在在哪里？

column1: Hypotheses arise by guesswork, or by inspiration, but having been formulated they can and must be tested rigorously, using the appropriate methodology.
column2: 假设可能源于猜测或灵感，但一旦形成，就必须用适当的方法进行严格检验。

column1: If the predictions you make as a result of deducing certain consequences from your hypothesis are not shown to be correct then you discard or modify your hypothesis.
column2: 如果从假设中推导出的预测未被证实为正确，你就舍弃或修改该假设。
column4: as a result of|prep. 结果

column1: If the predictions turn out to be correct then your hypothesis has been supported and may be retained until such time as some further test shows it not to be correct.
column2: 如果预测结果被证实为正确，你的假设就得到了支持，可以保留，直到有新的测试表明它不正确为止。
column4: turn out|v. 被证实为正确

column1: Once you have arrived at your hypothesis, which is a product of your imagination, you then proceed to a strictly logical and rigorous process, based upon deductive argument — hence the term ‘hypothetico-deductive’.
column2: 一旦你得出了自己的假设——这个假设其实是你想象力的产物——那么接下来你就需要经历一个严格的逻辑推理过程，这一过程基于演绎推理的原理。因此，这种思维方式被称为‘假设-演绎法’。

column1: So don’t worry if you have some idea of what your results will tell you before you even begin to collect data; there are no scientists in existence who really wait until they have all the evidence in front of them before they try to work out what it might possibly mean.
column2: 所以，即使在你开始收集数据之前就已经知道结果会告诉你什么，也无需担心——世上根本不存在科学家会等到所有证据都摆在面前，才去尝试推测这些证据可能意味着什么。

column1: The closest we ever get to this situation is when something happens by accident; but even then the researcher has to formulate a hypothesis to be tested before being sure that, for example, a mould might prove to be a successful antidote to bacterial infection.
column2: 我们最接近这种情况的情形是某事偶然发生；但即便如此，研究人员仍必须先提出一个假设进行检验，才能确信，例如霉菌可能成为细菌感染的有效解毒剂。

column1: The myth of scientific method is not only that it is inductive (which we have seen is incorrect) but also that the hypothetico-deductive method proceeds in a step-by-step, inevitable fashion.
column2: 科学方法的神话不仅在于它被认为是归纳性的（我们已看到这是错误的），还在于人们误以为假设—演绎法是按步骤、不可避免地进行的。

column1: The hypothetico-deductive method describes the logical approach to much research work, but it does not describe the psychological behaviour that brings it about.
column2: 假设-演绎法描述了科学研究中所采用的逻辑途径，但并未说明引发这一途径的心理行为。

column1: This is much more holistic — involving guesses, reworkings, corrections, blind alleys and above all inspiration, in the deductive as well as the hypothetic component -than is immediately apparent from reading the final thesis or published papers.
column2: 这其实是一种更为全面的方法——涉及到猜测、修改、修正，以及灵感的产生。这种过程既包括演绎性的思考，也包括假设性的探索。从最终的研究成果或已发表的论文来看，似乎并不容易理解这种整体性的方法。

column1: These have been, quite properly, organised into a more serial, logical order so that the worth of the output may be evaluated independently of the behavioural processes by which it was obtained.
column2: 这些成果已经按照一种更为有序、逻辑清晰的方式进行了整理，这样一来，就可以独立于获取这些成果所采用的行为过程来评价它们的价值了。

column1: It is the difference, for example between the academic papers with which Crick and Watson demonstrated the structure of the DNA molecule and the fascinating book The Double Helix in which Watson (1968) described how they did it.
column2: 例如，克里克和沃森通过学术论文揭示了DNA分子的结构，而沃森（1968）在《双螺旋》一书中则描述了他们是如何做到的。

column1: From this point of view, ‘scientific method’ may more usefully be thought of as a way of writing up research rather than as a way of carrying it out.
column2: 从这个角度来看，所谓的‘科学方法’更应被理解为一种撰写研究报告的方式，而不是进行研究的手段。
